subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@finedge.com>, Rajesh Kapoor <rajesh.kapoor@finedge.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation

Hi Samantha / Rajesh,

Thanks again for taking the time today - really appreciate the open discussion. Below is a short recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned.

TL;DR (what we heard)
- Pain: two recent incidents where the model inference layer caused production errors and elevated latency across critical flows.
- Impact: customer-facing features degraded (search/autocomplete) during ~20 minutes; elevated error rates resulted in manual rollbacks.
- Current stack: FinEdge runs a mix of GCP-hosted endpoints and an in-house proxy that routes traffic to model backends; keys managed in your KMS.
- Needs: predictable failover, audit-level logs/traces, clear SLOs/SLA for inference, and a way to degrade gracefully (fallback model/region) without user-visible errors.

Success criteria you mentioned
- Availability: 99.9% inference availability for critical routes
- Latency: p95 < 200ms, p99 < 500ms under normal load (we discussed relaxed p99 for very spiky tails)
- Auditability: request-level audit logs retained for 90 days; detailed error traces for top failures
- Security: support for KMS/HSM-backed keys and per-tenant encryption controls

What Redwood can immediately help with (high level)
- Multi-region routing + automated fallback policies (region-level failover)
- Fallback model strategies: quantized smaller model or a lightweight reranking model to preserve UX while reducing cost and failure surface
- Prefix/KV caching to reduce p99 latency and mitigate spikes
- Request-level tracing and exportable audit logs; can integrate with your SIEM

Attachments: I've attached our reliability_playbook.pdf and a rough Dedicated pricing worksheet (redwood-dedicated-pricing.xlsx) to give a sense of cost for reserved capacity and failover setups.

Next steps (proposed)
1) Share SOC2 / security questionnaire and confirm HSM/KMS requirements (I'll attach our SOC2 report once I have a secure channel).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra team + our reliability engineer (please share availability next week).
3) Draft a mutual action plan that lays out SLAs, rollouts, and minimal viable fallbacks (I'll start a draft and share).

Do I have this right? Anything I missed or mischaracterized?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@finedge.com>

Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 17:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation

Thanks Marissa - this is great and captures the conversation well. A couple of clarifications / extra context from our side: 

- Incident history: we had a major incident on 2026-05-02 where the model inference cluster in us-central suffered a full node outage, which caused the proxy to route traffic to a cold pool with degraded models. The outage lasted ~18 minutes; our monitoring showed a spike in 500s and a p99 latency around 1.2s.
- We also had a smaller incident on 2026-04-10 related to autoscaling where queueing led to timeouts for async requests.
- Requirements: HSM-backed key wrapping for model encryption is a hard requirement (we operate in fintech). Also need per-request audit logs and signed timestamps.

A couple of asks for the next call:
- Can you walk through how Redwood handles a primary-region failure (automated failover, traffic draining, cache warm-up)?
- In the fallback model scenario, how do you handle quality regressions? We need configurable thresholds and an automatic rollback path.

We're available Tue/Wed next week (PST) for the technical deep-dive.

Samantha

I'll propose two slots Tue 10:00-10:45am PST and Wed 2:00-2:45pm PST - please confirm which works and I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks - I'll take point on the deep-dive. Quick notes from an engineering perspective: 

- We can support HSM-backed key wrapping (we integrate with Cloud HSM + customer-owned HSMs via standard KMIP flows).
- Failover pattern we typically recommend: active-region with warm standby(s) + asynchronous cache pre-warm on failover; traffic is routed via smart router with circuit-breakers and graceful draining.
- Fallback model approach: primary full model -> quantized/float16 variant -> tiny reranker. We attach quality gates based on evaluation sets and live-sampling; if quality drops below threshold we automatically route a percentage to the primary until metrics recover.

For the deep-dive please send:
- A redacted trace sample or p95/p99 histograms for the critical route
- Any constraints around data residency we should know about

Agenda I'll cover: architecture diagram, failover timeline (expected recovery windows), cache warm-up strategy, and where logs/traces are emitted. I've started a shared MAP doc here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-reliability-m-a-p - I'll add a section on fallbacks.

-Jonas
